The road is closed. Dinner will still be served.

Snowed In is a printable murder-mystery dinner for 8–12 adults. Guests do not wear costumes. They sit down to a holiday meal at a snowbound lodge, read a short character booklet, and talk. One of them already knows what happened. The rest of the table can solve it fairly — without a shock twist that was never clued.

This is an instant digital download. Nothing will be shipped. Print at home or at a copy shop on ordinary US Letter paper.

WHAT YOU GET
• A spoiler-free host guide, with a two-hour evening timeline and casting for 8–12
• 12 character booklets (8 required roles, 4 optional — add or drop in a set order)
• Round 1 and Round 2 clue cards, plus envelope labels
• Printable invitations and cut-apart name tags

• An optional “next party” thank-you page

• A Start Here guide so you know what to print for the table and what to keep sealed

HOW THE EVENING RUNS
About 2 to 2½ hours, including a relaxed dinner. You may host from the outside, or play along as a character. If you play along, one booklet includes a folded private panel — it is clearly marked. Hand that booklet to a guest and leave the sealed ending unopened until accusations are finished.

No costumes are required. A holiday sweater, a dress, or a clean shirt is enough.

WHO IT IS FOR
Adults 18 and older. The story includes a death (described, not graphic), money trouble, a family secret, and a cover-up. It is written as a talky, clue-driven dinner, not a scare and not a roast. It is not written for children or mixed-age family tables.

WHY THIS KIT
• Fair: a careful table can reach the right person, including if an optional guest is missing
• Kind to the host: spoiler-free setup, a sealed ending, and a host-plays-along path
• Kind to the table: no gore, no costume pressure, and planted trails that were meant to be walked
• Ready tonight: print, cut, and set two envelopes aside

DETAILS
• Players: 8–12 adults
• Time: 2–2½ hours
• Pages: print only what you need; booklets, cards, invitations, and name tags are in split files
• Paper: US Letter. Color looks best; black and white is playable
• Skill level: none. If you can host a dinner, you can host this

Please do not share the files in a group drive or reprint them for another host. This purchase is for your household or the party you are hosting.

Questions before you print? Send a message. Thank you for taking Hartwell Lodge for the night.

THE COMPANY LINE
A Printable Office Holiday Murder Mystery for 8–20 Adults

The Company Line is a printable office holiday murder mystery game for 8–20 adults—an evidence-driven corporate party mystery with low-pressure role-play, optional audio moments, and a near-blind host who can play.

8–20 total participants | 90–120 minutes | Printable + digital files | No scripts to memorize | Near-blind participating host

Welcome aboard The Renshaw Special.

What begins as a polished company holiday retreat aboard a private winter rail charter takes a darker turn when Claire Nolan is found dead.

As workplace history, conflicting accounts, missing source material, and a carefully managed company story begin to unravel, your group must determine what really happened.

Players investigate through private character information, natural conversation, staged evidence, and a final accusation—not mandatory speeches, accents, or theatrical performances.

THE EXPERIENCE

The Company Line is built for adults who want to investigate rather than perform.

There are no memorized scripts, no required character voices, and no expectation that everyone spend the evening giving dramatic speeches. Players read their private information, talk naturally, compare evidence, question one another, and decide what they believe.

The mystery unfolds in controlled rounds. New evidence changes the meaning of information the group already has, giving players a reason to revisit assumptions and reconsider earlier theories.

Your host follows a clear release system while the group does the actual solving.

WHAT’S INCLUDED

Your digital game includes:

20 individual character packets, each with a complete 7-page private packet and guided round progression

Combined 140-page character packet print master

Near-blind Host System

START HERE Guide

Character Assignment Guide

Step-by-step Host Dashboard

Print + Assembly Guide

Evidence-release labels

E01–E10 evidence system with realistic records, working documents, event materials, statements, and timeline evidence

2 optional audio files in MP3 format

Exact printed transcript fallback for both audio moments

Final Accusation Sheets

Sealed Final Reconstruction

Pre-party invitation + player note

Character name tents

Cocktail menu

Mocktail menu

Host drink-pour guide

Spotify playlist guide + QR card

Atmosphere + dress guide

Welcome Aboard sign

Welcome + Access Guide with organized game-file access

PLAYER COUNT

This game supports 8–20 total participants, including the participating host.

An 8-player game means eight people total—not eight players plus a separate host.

Characters 01–08 form the core cast. For larger groups, additional characters are added in a controlled order through Character 20, so the mystery remains complete and workable at every supported player count.

HOST CAN PLAY

Host can play—no separate game master required.

The Company Line uses a near-blind host system, which means the organizer can take a character and participate in the mystery without reading the murderer reveal in advance.

The host manages the timing of evidence releases and keeps the evening moving with the spoiler-light Host Dashboard. The sealed Final Reconstruction remains closed until every player has committed a final accusation.

DO WE HAVE TO ACT?

Not unless you want to.

This mystery is intentionally designed for low-pressure role-play and low improvisation.

You do not need:

Memorized scripts

Character voices

Formal speeches

Acting experience

Character-specific costumes

Players can read carefully, talk with one another, ask questions, share what they know when appropriate, and investigate the case.

That makes The Company Line especially well suited to office and corporate gatherings where guests may have very different comfort levels with traditional role-playing games.

HOW THE GAME WORKS

Before the party, the host assigns characters and prints only the packets needed for the final group size.

Guests begin with private character information and public retreat materials.

After the murder is announced, evidence is released in stages.

Each round adds new information, challenges earlier assumptions, and gives players fresh reasons to question what happened both tonight and in the company’s past.

At the end, every player or team privately commits to a final theory before the sealed reconstruction is opened.

The solution is designed to come from evidence convergence rather than one magic clue.

PERFECT FOR

Office holiday parties

Corporate Christmas parties

Company celebrations

Corporate team-building events

Employee appreciation parties

End-of-year office gatherings

Workplace holiday dinners

Winter retreats

Adult friend groups

Adult family gatherings

Mystery and deduction-game fans

Although The Company Line works beautifully as a Christmas-party activity, its setting is a sophisticated winter holiday retreat—not a campy Christmas game with Santa, elves, or North Pole characters.

STYLE + TONE

Think:

Private winter rail retreat

Upscale hospitality setting

Workplace secrets and professional pressure

Realistic evidence

Layered motives

A genuine case to investigate

The tone is adult, polished, atmospheric, and workplace-appropriate.

RUNTIME

Plan for approximately 90–120 minutes.

The Host Dashboard uses flexible conversation milestones rather than rigid timers. A highly social group can take a little longer, while a focused investigative group may move more quickly.

PRINTING

Files are designed primarily for US Letter printing.

Each active player receives one 7-page character packet.

For shared evidence:

8–12 participants: Print 1 complete evidence set

13–20 participants: Print 2 identical evidence sets for easier table access

You do not need to print every included file. The Print + Assembly Guide identifies exactly what is required and what is optional.

OPTIONAL AUDIO

Two optional audio moments are included to add atmosphere and support the investigation.

Audio is not required to solve the mystery.

A complete transcript is included for each audio cue, so the host can read the wording aloud if audio is unavailable or if the group prefers not to use it.

DIGITAL PRODUCT INFORMATION

This is a digital product. No physical item will be mailed.

After purchase, download the Welcome + Access PDF from Etsy. It provides access to the organized customer game files, including the printable PDFs and optional audio materials.

Because this is a mystery game, please avoid opening the sealed Final Reconstruction or reading another player’s private packet before play.

Files are for personal use only. Purchase does not include commercial reproduction, resale, redistribution, or sharing of the digital files outside your event group.

A NOTE ABOUT GROUP STYLE

The Company Line was made for adults who like the idea of a murder mystery but may not love traditional dinner-theater games.

Your group can dress up and lean into the characters—or sit around a table with drinks, investigate documents, debate the timeline, and accuse their colleagues or friends of murder.

That flexibility is intentional.

GROUP SIZE AND FORMAT
8–20 coworkers share up to 10 character roles; at 20 players, every role is a pair. A separate host leads the game as Detective Frost. Allow 60–75 minutes. The story is non-graphic but includes planned layoffs and a poisoned boss. For an office event that avoids murder, see The Holly Ball Heist. A printable office party game for 8 to 20 coworkers: a holiday murder mystery that fits a long lunch or an afternoon party in 60 to 75 minutes. Teams work the clues together, nobody has to act, and it stays office friendly from start to finish. Then Preston Vale, the Chief Efficiency Officer who planned to announce a round of cuts at 1:00, is found slumped over his desk. Someone put mouse bait in his peppermint cocoa.

The badge log says Santa went into his office at 12:44. The livestream says Santa was in the Big Room the whole time. So who was the other Santa?

Murder at Merriwell & Finch is a complete printable murder mystery game made for the office holiday party. It plays in 60 to 75 minutes, so it fits a long lunch, a team event or an afternoon party, and it works for 8 to 20 players.

WHAT'S INCLUDED (114 pages)
- Host guide (16 pages): setup, casting, a timeline for a full game (about 75 minutes) or an express game (about 60 minutes), a read-aloud script for every round, nudges if the room gets stuck, and checklists
- Invitations: a printable design (two per page) and a dark digital version, all with editable fields
- Casting cards for every character
- 10 character booklets, 4 pages each: backstory, secret, goals, what to share each round, costume ideas and an editable "played by" line
- 10 sealed cards, so even the killer only finds out at the start of the game
- 15 clue cards across three rounds, plus 2 for the 10-character game
- 12 evidence props: a floor plan, the run of show, a badge log, two emails, the livestream chat, the boss's notes, the office newsletter, a petty cash IOU, a sales order, a printer log and a repair invoice
- Suspect worksheet and accusation ballots, with a scoring table
- Solution script for the host to read aloud, and an envelope to fold and seal it in
- 16 name tags with editable "played by" lines, and 6 award certificates (editable)

HOW IT PLAYS
1. Send the invitations and casting cards a few days ahead, so people can find an ugly sweater.
2. On the day, the host plays Detective Frost of the Mistlewick Police, deals out the clue cards round by round and has each piece of evidence read aloud. Players question each other and give up their secrets.
3. Each player or team fills in a ballot: who did it, how they got into the office, what proves it and why.
4. Open the envelope, read the solution, score the ballots and hand out the awards.

The host doesn't need to know the answer, so you can play along. Clue cards are always true, and only the killer may lie. The case can be solved from the clue cards and evidence alone.

PLAYER COUNT AND TEAMS
- 8 or 9 players: use the 8 core characters (with 9, one character is played by a pair)
- 10 to 20 players: use all 10 characters, and pair players up as the group grows. At 20, every character is played by a team of two
- Teams share one sealed card and one ballot, and each teammate gets their own booklet. Great for shy colleagues and new starters
- Every role can be played by anyone. The characters are written so gender never matters

OFFICE FRIENDLY
- A mild, silly "murder": a poisoned mug of cocoa, nothing graphic
- No drinking, no romance, no gambling, no swearing
- The secrets are classic office sins: a fake sales order, a cat living in the supply closet, a borrowed petty cash fund and an anonymous joke newsletter
- An original fictional company. No real brands or people
- Tips for remote and hybrid teams are in the host guide

FILES

This bundle holds three printable murder mystery games for the holiday season, each a logic elimination puzzle: read the clues, cross suspects off the register, and find the one killer. Three holidays, three stories, three killers: 54 clues and 6,000 records in all.

THE THREE GAMES

1. Murder at Wrenfield House. Thanksgiving Day, 1926. The host's cider was poisoned at the head table, the gates are shut until the lieutenant says so, and the killer is one of the 2,000 names in the guest book.

2. Murder at Merriwether's. Christmas Eve, 1954. The owner's punch was poisoned, the department store is locked until morning, and the killer is one of the 2,000 names on the guest list.

3. Murder at the Midnight Ball. New Year's Eve, 1949. The host's tea was poisoned on the bandstand, the elevators are stopped, and the killer is one of the 2,000 names on the door list.

Each game stands alone, with its own story, register and killer. Play one for each holiday or all three in one weekend, solo or as a team.

THE BUNDLE PRICE

Each of these three games is also sold on its own in my shop. This bundle costs less than buying the three separately.

WHAT'S INCLUDED (3 ZIP files, instant download)

One ZIP file per game. Each ZIP holds the same three files as that game's own listing:

• Puzzle PDF, US Letter: illustrated story, how to play, the clues, a Clue Guide and the register.
• Solution PDF: a separate file with a spoiler warning page up front, then the killer, the motive, how many people should remain after each clue, and a short thank-you note from the shop.
• Answer Checker: an HTML file you open in a web browser. It works offline: no internet, no account, no spoilers.

Game by game:

• Murder at Wrenfield House: 77-page Puzzle PDF, 18 clues, a 5-page Clue Guide and a 67-page guest book of 2,000 guests.
• Murder at Merriwether's: 77-page Puzzle PDF, 18 clues, a 5-page Clue Guide and a 67-page guest list of 2,000 guests.
• Murder at the Midnight Ball: 77-page Puzzle PDF, 18 clues, a 5-page Clue Guide and a 67-page door list of 2,000 guests.

On a computer, double-click a ZIP file to unzip it.

WHAT MAKES THESE DIFFERENT

• Check your answer without spoilers. Each game has its own Answer Checker: start typing a name, pick it from the list, and get "Correct!" or "Not this one - look again." The full solution stays in its own file until you want it.
• Computer-verified: in every game, the clues leave exactly one name, and removing any single clue would leave more than one.
• Clues about the world, not word games. The clues are about ages, occupations, hair, and where people were at the key moment of the day. No counting letters in names.
• A Clue Guide in every game shows how to apply each clue, with Keep and Cross-out examples taken from real records in the register.
• Illustrated story pages set the scene before the first clue.

HOW TO PLAY

1. Read a clue.
2. Cross people off the register.
3. One name left - that's your killer. Check it without spoilers.

A printer and a pencil are all you need. The register pages print on a white background. Prefer screens? The PDFs work on a screen too.

Thanksgiving weekend, Christmas Eve, New Year's Eve at home, game nights, date nights, and gifts for mystery lovers and puzzle solvers. No app and no subscription.
